description: A single-panel XPS (X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy) figure, labelled (a). It plots the Fe 2p core-level region as Intensity (a. u.) on the y-axis (no numeric scale printed) against Binding energy (eV) on the x-axis, ticked every 2 eV from 704 to 720 eV, with binding energy increasing to the left. A black experimental envelope curve is maximum between the 710 and 712 eV tick marks and tails down towards 704 eV; a faint orange/pink tail extends under the envelope. Beneath the envelope, three shaded fitted components are drawn: a broad violet/purple peak labelled Fe2+, the tallest of the three, centred between 710 and 712 eV; a pink peak labelled Fe3+_OX at slightly higher binding energy (near 712 eV); and a small green peak labelled Fe3+_met near 713.5 eV. Arrows point from each label to its component. No sample name, composition, solution-treatment condition, scale bar or numeric intensity is printed on the panel, so the figure demonstrates only the spectral deconvolution: the Fe 2p envelope of the studied surface resolves into Fe2+ (dominant), Fe3+_OX and Fe3+_met contributions, indicating a mixed-valence Fe oxide film.

subfigures.description: XPS Fe 2p spectrum: black envelope curve plotted as Intensity (a. u.) vs Binding energy (eV) from 704 to 720 eV (2 eV ticks, axis reversed). Three shaded deconvoluted components with arrows and labels: Fe2+ (violet, tallest), Fe3+_OX (pink), Fe3+_met (green, smallest). No numeric intensity scale and no sample label are printed.

observations.observation: The figure consists of one panel only, labelled (a), and is an XPS spectrum of the Fe 2p region.
The x-axis is labelled 'Binding energy (eV)' and spans 704 to 720 eV with tick marks every 2 eV; the axis is plotted with increasing binding energy to the left.
The y-axis is labelled 'Intensity (a. u.)' and carries no numeric tick values.
Three shaded fitted components are drawn and labelled by arrows: 'Fe2+' (violet/purple), 'Fe3+_OX' (pink) and 'Fe3+_met' (green).
The Fe2+ component is the largest-amplitude fitted peak, while the Fe3+_met component is the smallest.
The black experimental envelope curve reaches its maximum between the 710 and 712 eV tick marks.
The Fe3+_OX fitted component is positioned at higher binding energy than the Fe2+ component, and the Fe3+_met component lies at still higher binding energy (near 713.5 eV).
No sample name, alloy composition, grain size or solution-treatment temperature is printed anywhere on the panel.
No scale bar, magnification or numeric peak-area/atomic-percentage values are printed on the figure.
No caption was extracted for this figure, so the sample identity and measurement conditions are not stated in the supplied metadata.
